blocks.text: Noah’s fingers wrapped around my wrist so tightly I could feel every tiny knuckle pressing into my skin.
The kitchen smelled like meatloaf, melted butter, and green beans that had been sitting beneath the warm light too long.
My son Tyler froze beside the dining table with his fork still in his hand.
The old wall clock kept ticking as if nothing unusual was happening.
But my six-year-old nephew was staring at me like something terrible was about to happen.
“Noah,” I whispered, “what are you talking about?”
I had never seen that expression on a child before.
Something about Noah’s words made the room suddenly feel much colder.
I didn’t know what was happening, but I knew one thing.
“Okay,” I whispered. “We’re going outside.”
We slipped through the back door and hurried into the bushes along the side of the house.
I pulled both boys down behind a thick hedge.
For nearly five minutes, nothing happened.
I began wondering whether Noah had simply misunderstood something.
Then headlights appeared at the end of our driveway.
A dark sedan slowly rolled toward the house.
Neither one looked around like a normal visitor.
They walked straight toward my front door.
Then I saw something that made my stomach drop.
I wanted to ask more, but suddenly a light flickered inside the house.
They knew exactly where they were going.
After several terrifying minutes, one man said something.
They knew I was supposed to be in the house.
Before I could ask anything else, the back door opened.
He stood there for several seconds, looking around.
Then he walked toward the exact spot where we were hiding.
Noah buried his face against my shoulder.
After a moment, he turned and walked back into the house.
Noah’s father—my older brother Daniel—had dropped Noah off at my house five days earlier for summer vacation.
Daniel had told me he needed to work out of town.
But I never imagined anything like this.
“Because he said you wouldn’t believe me.”
“They said Aunt Emma had something they needed.”
“My daddy said you don’t know you have it.”
Before I could respond, the front door suddenly slammed.
We waited until the taillights disappeared.
Officers arrived shortly afterward and searched the house.
My kitchen floor was covered with papers.
And one envelope with my name written across it.
On the back of the photograph was a handwritten message:
“The truth was never supposed to reach Emma.”
One officer asked if I recognized the documents.
He pointed toward an old wooden cabinet in the hallway.
Inside was a USB drive, several photographs, and a handwritten letter.
It said that years earlier, my father had discovered that someone had been secretly stealing money from a family business.
But before he could expose the person responsible, he became seriously ill.
The evidence had been hidden inside the house.
And the person responsible was someone the family trusted.
One showed my father standing beside a man.
The date on the photograph was fifteen years earlier.
Daniel had always told me he knew nothing about my father’s investigation.
“Daddy knew about the box,” he whispered.
Noah reached into the pocket of his pajamas.
Daniel hadn’t sent Noah to me because he needed childcare.
He had sent Noah because he knew something was happening.
But why would he put his own son in the middle of it?
The officer immediately asked me to put the phone on speaker.
But before anyone could say another word, another notification appeared.
